q: Predict the lifecycle log when activity A starts an opaque activity B and the user then presses Back.
a: A onPause; B onCreate, onStart, onResume; A onStop. On Back: B onPause; A onRestart, onStart, onResume; B onStop, onDestroy.
explanation: The outgoing activity pauses first, but stops only after the new one is visible so the transition never shows an empty window. B is finished on Back, so it is destroyed, while A restarts instead of being recreated. If B were translucent or a dialog theme, A would only pause because it stays partly visible.
mistake: Saying A is stopped before B is created, or that A is recreated when it returns.
rubric: A pauses before B is created
A stops only after B resumes
A uses onRestart rather than onCreate on return
B is stopped and destroyed after A resumes
Mentions how a translucent B changes the result
followups: What changes if B uses a dialog theme?
Where does onSaveInstanceState run, and why does it matter?

q: Fix the fragment that crashes after returning from a detail screen and loses its scroll position when orders update.
a: Collect with viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycleScope plus repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED), and create one ListAdapter per view and submitList updates.
explanation: lifecycleScope belongs to the fragment, which outlives its view on the back stack. The collector keeps running after onDestroyView and reads a null binding, causing a crash. Every new view also launches another collector. repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED) on the view lifecycle stops collection in the background and restarts it on return. Replacing the adapter on every emission resets scroll position and redraws everything; a ListAdapter with DiffUtil applies minimal changes.
mistake: Switching only to launchWhenStarted, which suspends rather than cancels collection and keeps upstream work alive.
rubric: Uses the view lifecycle owner, not the fragment lifecycle
Uses repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED)
Explains the crash on the null binding
Reuses one adapter and calls submitList
Mentions duplicate collectors
followups: How would you collect the same flow in Compose?

q: Write a SearchViewModel that debounces typing, cancels outdated searches, handles errors, and survives process death.
a: Store the query in SavedStateHandle, then debounce, trim, distinctUntilChanged, flatMapLatest to the repository with catch inside, and expose the result with stateIn.
explanation: debounce waits for typing to pause, distinctUntilChanged skips repeated queries, and flatMapLatest cancels the previous search when a new query arrives. Put catch inside flatMapLatest: outside it, one failure would end the whole stream. SavedStateHandle.getStateFlow restores the query after process death. Combine the raw query with results so the text field updates immediately while the search itself is debounced. stateIn with WhileSubscribed(5_000) keeps the search alive during rotation.
mistake: Calling catch on the outer flow, so the first network error permanently stops search.
rubric: Debounces and removes duplicate queries
Cancels outdated searches with flatMapLatest
Handles a blank query without calling the repository
Catches errors per search without ending the stream
Restores the query with SavedStateHandle
Exposes a StateFlow with stateIn
followups: How would you unit test the 300 ms debounce?
How would you keep the previous results visible while loading?

q: Write the reduce(state, event) function for a feed screen's ViewModel that keeps visible content during refresh failures.
a: Use an exhaustive when over sealed events: Refresh marks Content as refreshing, Loaded replaces state, Failed keeps Content with a one-off message or becomes Error, and MessageShown clears the message.
explanation: A pure reducer keeps screen rules in one testable function with no Android dependencies. The key decision is to keep content the user can already see when a refresh fails, showing a snackbar message instead of a full-screen error. Clearing the message after it is shown prevents the snackbar from reappearing after rotation. Sealed types with an exhaustive when make the compiler flag a missing case when a new event is added.
mistake: Replacing visible content with a full-screen error on a failed refresh.
rubric: Writes a pure function with an exhaustive when
Keeps content and stops refreshing on failure
Shows a one-off message and clears it
Returns to Loading from Error on refresh
Explains how this is tested without Android
followups: How would you connect this reducer to a StateFlow in the ViewModel?
How would you handle pagination events?

q: Write the WorkManager setup and worker that sync offline note edits safely, without duplicates or lost edits.
a: A CoroutineWorker drains dirty notes in batches with idempotent upserts and revision-checked markSynced, retries transient errors, and is scheduled as unique KEEP work with constraints plus a unique periodic job.
explanation: Unique work with KEEP collapses many edit triggers into one sync. Because a running worker ignores new KEEP requests, the worker loops until no dirty notes remain. markSynced clears dirty only when the local revision is unchanged, so an edit made during the upload is not lost. Device-generated IDs make the upload idempotent, and the base version lets the server detect conflicts. Transient failures return Result.retry() with exponential backoff, while 4xx validation errors are recorded for the user and excluded from the loop. A unique periodic request covers missed triggers.
mistake: Marking a note synced unconditionally, which loses an edit made while it was uploading.
rubric: Uses unique work so syncs do not overlap
Sets network and battery constraints
Uses idempotent uploads with device IDs
Prevents losing edits made during the upload
Separates retryable errors from permanent ones
Schedules a unique periodic sync
followups: How would you resolve a conflict when the server version moved ahead?
How would you show sync status in the UI?
What changes if a sync must run immediately and the user is waiting?
